To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Pitzer ion interaction parameters for the NaOH H 2O system were determined from the literature and the new set of interaction parameters can be used for the Na+ Li+ OH H2O quaternary system to very high concentration and temperature ranges.
the NaOH H20 system is partially dissociated, and that the new parameters for this system, which are valid up to 523.5 K, are consistent with previous parameters for NaCl and LiOH.

a new set of parameters was derived for the binary system NaOH H2 O and that these parameters can be used in the description of the three ternary systems NaCl NaOH H2 0, LiOH NaOH H2 and Na+ Li+ OH Cl H2O, to high concentrations and temperatures, including the solubility of NaOH(cr) up to saturation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new Pitzer model for the NaOH H20 system and its extension to the ternary systems NaCl H20, LiOH H20, NaOH NaCl, NaOH LiOH, NaOH NaOH H20, LiCl H20, and NaOH NaCl LiOH.
the development of a thermodynamic model for the NaOH H20 system, and its application to the NaOH NaCl LiOH H20 systems.
the development of a thermodynamic model to represent the properties of aqueous NaOH and NaOH containing systems at high temperatures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the present set of Pitzer parameters provides an excellent description of the properties of the four systems NaOH H2 O, NaOH NaOH NaCl LiOH H2 O and NaOH NaCl NaLi OH H2 O, from 273 K to 573 K and at saturated vapour pressure, for concentrations up to the solid salt saturation limit of NaOH.

our new set of PIM parameters for the binary and ternary systems Na+ Cl H2O Na+ Li+ OH H2O NaOH H2Os and NaOH NaCl LiOH H2Os is the best set of parameters currently available in the literature for the description of these aqueous systems.
the present study is the most complete and reliable description of the properties of these three systems to date.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the new Pitzer parameters for the NaOH H20 system and for the ternary systems NaCl H20 NaOH and LiOH H20 NaOH are able to describe the phase behavior of all four systems at temperatures up to 523. 15 K and concentrations up to 30 mol* kg1 with an accuracy of 0.1 K and 0.1 molal.

the present study provides a consistent set of parameters for the quaternary electrolyte Na+ Li+ H+ Cl OH HCO3 SO4 2 H2O system, which covers all possible combinations of these ions, including the formation of solid NaCl and LiCl salts, at concentrations up to over the solid salt saturation limit and over the temperature range from 273.2 to 523.2 K, for pressures up to saturated vapor pressure, for the first time.

the new Pitzer parameters are able to describe with good accuracy the phase diagram of the quaternary system Na+ Li+ NaOH H2 O, the phase diagram of two ternary NaOH based systems and the boiling point elevation of NaOH in the binary system up to 523. 15K, at concentrations up to saturation of solid NaOH and at saturated vapor pressure.
The main takeaway from our work is that

it is necessary to take the partial dissociation of electrolytes into account in order to obtain a good representation of the properties of electrolyte solutions over wide ranges of temperature and concentration.
the Pitzer model is a very powerful tool for the description of electrolytes, especially at high temperatures and concentrations.
the Pitzer ion interaction approach, when applied with the right parameters, can be used to describe a wide variety of aqueous systems with a very high degree of accuracy.
